newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Optus Vision completes A$700 mln debt raising.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Optus Vision completes A$700 mln debt raising.

text.p: Australian pay television Optus Vision said on Tuesday that it had completed an A$700 million funding facility with a group of banks.
"The funding is an increase and extension of the A$280 million short term debt facility completed in February this year," Optus Vision chief financial officer Mike Buckling said in a statement.
"However, the latest arrangement is seen by all parties as the forerunner of a larger long-term facility which we expect to complete in the first half of 1997," Buckling said.
"The banks have completed a major review of all aspects of our business, together with ongoing related issues, and have strongly vindicated our long-term business strategy," he said.
Optus Vision said the debt facility was arranged with Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd, Deutsche Bank AG and Toronto Dominion Australia Ltd.

The pay television operator said Zygmunt Switkowski the chief executive officer of Optus Communications Pty Ltd, which owns 46.5 percent of Optus Vision, will become executive chairman of the pay TV group.

Optus Vision said Switkowski will work closely with Optus Vision's chief operating officer Frank Anthony pending the appointment of a new chief executive officer following the resignation of former chief Geoffrey Cousins.
Optus Vision is also 46.5 percent owned by Continental CableVision Inc, which has merged with U.S. West.
The balance of Optus Vision is owned by Seven Network Ltd and Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd.
